denomProfiles/church-of-the-lord-aladura: Yoruba "praying church" of fasting, prophecy and revealed holy names.
Faith in the Triune God and Christ, with Scripture as the Word of God.
Prayer as the key to salvation, healing and protection.
Revelation through visions, dreams and prophecy, including holy names given to the founder.
Holiness and purity of life.
Prayer and fasting.
Healing without medicine or traditional charms.
Prophecy and spiritual guidance.
Mission in West Africa and the diaspora.
The annual Taborah festival on Mount Taborah, Ogere.
White robes and removal of shoes in worship.
Use of psalms, holy water and holy names in prayer.
Baptism and Holy Communion.
A hierarchy under a Primate; women may be ordained as ministers.
Aladura diaspora churches
Its British congregations were among the first African churches in Britain (1960s).
Ecumenical recognition of AICs
It joined the World Council of Churches in 1975.
Josiah Olunowo Ositelu
Founder and first Primate (d. 1966).
Emmanuel Owoade Adeleke Adejobi
Second Primate (1966–1991), who led its mission to Britain.
Rufus Okikiolaolu Ositelu
Primate from 1998.
denomProfiles/celestial-church-of-christ: White-robed, barefoot prophetic church founded by Samuel Oshoffa in Porto-Novo.
Faith in the Triune God and Christ, with Scripture as the Word of God.
Revelation through visions, prophecy and the Holy Spirit.
Rejection of idols, charms and traditional medicine.
Purity of life according to Old Testament norms.
Healing and protection through prayer.
Visions and prophecy.
Purity and holiness.
Mission in West Africa and the diaspora.
White soutanes and bare feet in worship.
Candles, incense, holy water and prayer at the beach.
Ban on pork, alcohol and tobacco.
Purity rules, including exclusion of menstruating women from the sanctuary.
Christmas pilgrimage to Imeko, Ogun State; men lead and women are not ordained.
West African diaspora
Celestial parishes spread to Europe and North America.
African Initiated Churches
It is one of the largest Aladura-type churches.
Samuel Bilewu Oshoffa
Founder and Pastor (d. 1985).
Alexander Abiodun Bada
Second Pastor (1985–2000).
denomProfiles/nazareth-baptist-church/ta: Zulu prophetic church of Isaiah Shembe, centred on Ekuphakameni and the holy mountain Nhlangakazi.
denomProfiles/nazareth-baptist-church/co: God revealed himself afresh to the Zulu people through the prophet Isaiah Shembe, whom members honour as a divinely sent messenger.
Scripture is read alongside Shembe's own hymns and teachings, which carry revelatory authority for members.
Strict observance of a Saturday Sabbath, following Old Testament law.
Healing comes through prayer, the prophet's blessing and obedience rather than medicine or traditional diviners.
Purity laws drawn from the Hebrew Bible govern food, dress and conduct.
denomProfiles/nazareth-baptist-church/fo: Restoring dignity and order to African life under colonial and apartheid pressure.
Holy places: Ekuphakameni and Nhlangakazi mountain as sacred sites of pilgrimage.
Continuity of leadership in Shembe's line.
denomProfiles/nazareth-baptist-church/pr: Annual January pilgrimage to Nhlangakazi and the July festival at Ekuphakameni.
Sacred dance (ukusina) in traditional and distinctive regalia as worship.
Worship barefoot, in white robes, on holy ground.
Singing from the hymnal Izihlabelelo zamaNazaretha composed largely by Isaiah and Galilee Shembe.
Baptism by immersion and a night-time communion with foot-washing.
denomProfiles/nazareth-baptist-church/in: The amaNazaretha became a classic case study for Bengt Sundkler's typology of 'Zionist' and 'Ethiopian' churches.
Shembe's hymns are recognised as foundational texts of modern isiZulu religious poetry.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/tagline: West African church born of William Wade Harris's 1913–15 preaching tour along the Ivorian coast.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/coreDoctrin: One God, proclaimed against fetishes and traditional cult objects, which converts were urged to burn.
Jesus Christ as Saviour and the Bible as God's word, received through Harris's preaching.
Harris as a prophet of the last days, called by the angel Gabriel in a Liberian prison cell (1910).
The Ten Commandments as the basis of Christian life.
Acceptance of polygamous families, which Harris did not require converts to break up.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/focuses/0: Mass conversion and baptism of coastal peoples of Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/focuses/1: Rejection of traditional ritual power and sorcery.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/focuses/2: A self-governing African church independent of missions.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/focuses/3: Preservation of Harris's teaching through preachers and 'apostles'.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/practices/0: Baptism with water as the sign of turning from fetishes to God.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/practices/1: Worship in white robes, with preachers carrying a cross and Bible as Harris did.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/practices/2: Singing of hymns composed in local languages.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/practices/3: Sunday rest and avoidance of alcohol in many congregations.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/influenced/: Many Harris converts joined Methodist missions arriving after 1924, giving that church its base.
A key early prophetic movement in the history of independent African Christianity.
denomProfiles/harrist-church/keyFigures/: Harris's appointed successor and organiser of the church
denomProfiles/local-churches/tagline: Chinese-rooted network holding one church per city, shaped by Watchman Nee and Witness Lee.
denomProfiles/local-churches/coreDoctrin: The church is one in each locality; denominational division is seen as contrary to the New Testament.
Salvation by grace through faith, followed by the believer's growth in the indwelling divine life.
God's economy: God dispensing himself into humanity to build up the Body of Christ.
Witness Lee's teaching that believers become God 'in life and nature but not in the Godhead'.
The Recovery Version of the Bible, with Lee's footnotes, as the movement's standard text.
denomProfiles/local-churches/focuses/0: Building up the local church as the practical expression of the Body of Christ.
denomProfiles/local-churches/focuses/1: Ministry publishing through Living Stream Ministry and Taiwan Gospel Book Room.
denomProfiles/local-churches/focuses/2: Every member functioning, without a separate clergy.
denomProfiles/local-churches/focuses/3: Spiritual life and the 'inner life' tradition of Nee's writings.
denomProfiles/local-churches/practices/0: Weekly Lord's Table meeting with breaking of bread.
denomProfiles/local-churches/practices/1: 'Calling on the name of the Lord' and 'pray-reading' Scripture.
denomProfiles/local-churches/practices/2: Mutual speaking and prophesying in meetings, led by elders rather than pastors.
denomProfiles/local-churches/practices/3: Large conferences and trainings, such as the semiannual training in Anaheim.
denomProfiles/local-churches/influenced/: Nee's books and the local-church pattern deeply shaped unregistered Chinese Protestantism.
Nee's 'The Normal Christian Life' and 'The Spiritual Man' became widely read evangelical classics.
denomProfiles/local-churches/keyFigures/: Co-worker and later leader in Taiwan and the United States (1905–1997)
denomProfiles/local-churches/inIndia: Local churches meet in a number of Indian cities, and Nee's books circulate widely among Indian evangelical and Brethren readers.
denomProfiles/three-self-patriotic-movem: China's state-registered Protestant body: self-governing, self-supporting, self-propagating and 'post-denominational'.
Historic Protestant faith in the Trinity, Christ's saving work and the authority of the Bible.
The 'three-self' principles of self-government, self-support and self-propagation, freeing Chinese churches from foreign control.
Patriotism and support for the People's Republic as part of Christian witness.
'Theological reconstruction' (from 1998) emphasising love and harmony with socialist society.
Post-denominational unity: former denominational differences are set aside in shared congregations.
Registered church life under the State Administration for Religious Affairs.
Training of pastors in seminaries such as Nanjing Union Theological Seminary.
Printing Bibles, notably through the Amity Printing Company in Nanjing.
'Sinicisation' of Christianity in line with official policy since 2015.
Sunday worship with sermon, hymns from the Chinese New Hymnal (1983) and prayer.
Both infant and believer's baptism, according to local custom.
Holy Communion celebrated in varied forms inherited from earlier missions.
Women widely ordained as pastors.
Chinese House Churches
Many unregistered congregations defined themselves by refusing to join the TSPM.
Ecumenical post-denominationalism
Its model has been discussed widely in world ecumenical circles.
Wu Yaozong (Y. T. Wu)
First chairman of the TSPM
K. H. Ting (Ding Guangxun)
Bishop, TSPM chairman and CCC president, leader of 'theological reconstruction'
Figure for Protestants in China given in the State Council white paper of April 2018; it refers mainly to registered churches and is widely regarded as a minimum.
denomProfiles/jesus-family/tagline: Pentecostal-style Christian commune founded by Jing Dianying in Mazhuang, Shandong.
denomProfiles/jesus-family/coreDoctrines: Salvation through Christ alongside a call to share all goods in common, as in Acts 2.
Direct experience of the Holy Spirit through visions, tongues and prophecy.
Self-denial and suffering as the path of discipleship.
denomProfiles/jesus-family/focuses/0: Communal living on farms and workshops as one 'family'.
denomProfiles/jesus-family/focuses/1: Care for the poor, disabled and outcast.
denomProfiles/jesus-family/focuses/2: Indigenous Chinese church life, independent of missions.
denomProfiles/jesus-family/practices/0: Common ownership of property and shared labour.
denomProfiles/jesus-family/practices/1: Long, emotional prayer meetings with weeping, tongues and dancing.
denomProfiles/jesus-family/practices/3: Strict authority of the family head, Jing Dianying.
denomProfiles/jesus-family/influenced/0/: Former members and its ethos of sacrifice and charismatic prayer fed later unregistered churches.
denomProfiles/oneness-pentecostal/taglin: Pentecostals who baptise 'in the name of Jesus' and teach God's oneness rather than three persons.
denomProfiles/oneness-pentecostal/coreDo: One God who reveals himself as Father, Son and Holy Spirit as modes or manifestations, not three persons.
Jesus is the name of God, and the fullness of the Godhead dwells in him bodily.
Water baptism must be by immersion in the name of Jesus Christ (Acts 2:38).
Spirit baptism with the evidence of speaking in tongues, which many bodies hold necessary for salvation.
Mainstream trinitarian churches regard this view as a form of modalism and reject it.
denomProfiles/oneness-pentecostal/focuse: Apostolic doctrine of Acts 2:38 as the full new-birth message.
denomProfiles/oneness-pentecostal/practi: Rebaptism of converts from trinitarian churches in Jesus' name.
Lively worship with tongues, prophecy and altar calls.
Modest dress and uncut hair for women in many churches.
denomProfiles/oneness-pentecostal/influe: The oldest surviving Oneness body, interracial from its early years.
Shares baptism in Jesus' name and Oneness theology.
denomProfiles/oneness-pentecostal/keyFig: Bishop and leader of the PAW
Evangelist and theologian of the movement
denomProfiles/oneness-pentecostal/inIndi: Oneness churches have a significant presence in North-East India, especially the United Pentecostal Church (North East India) in Mizoram, with smaller congregations in South India.
denomProfiles/latter-day-saints/tagline: Restorationist church founded by Joseph Smith, holding modern prophets and the Book of Mormon as scripture.
denomProfiles/latter-day-saints/coreDoct: The Godhead as three distinct beings: God the Father and Jesus Christ with glorified bodies, and the Holy Ghost.
A 'Great Apostasy' after the apostles, followed by the restoration of priesthood and church through Joseph Smith.
An open canon: the Bible, Book of Mormon, Doctrine and Covenants and Pearl of Great Price, guided by living prophets.
Eternal progression and exaltation: faithful humans may become like God.
Temple ordinances, including eternal marriage and proxy baptism for the dead.
Mainstream Christian churches do not regard its baptism as valid because of its non-Nicene teaching on God.
denomProfiles/latter-day-saints/focuses/: Missionary work by tens of thousands of young full-time missionaries.
denomProfiles/latter-day-saints/practice: Sunday sacrament meeting with bread and water blessed by priesthood holders.
Lay priesthood for worthy males from age 11 and a lay ministry of bishops.
Baptism by immersion at age eight or later.
The Word of Wisdom: abstinence from alcohol, tobacco, coffee and tea.
Tithing of ten per cent of income.
denomProfiles/latter-day-saints/influenc: The 'Reorganized' branch that rejected Brigham Young's leadership.
A major example of a new religious movement becoming a global church.
denomProfiles/latter-day-saints/keyFigur: Second president; led the migration to Utah
denomProfiles/latter-day-saints/members/: About 17.5 million members on record at the end of 2024, as reported in the Church's statistical report to the April 2025 General Conference.
denomProfiles/latter-day-saints/inIndia: Present in India since the 1850s with a small modern membership; the India Bengaluru Temple was announced in 2020.
